article.title: Proxmox bridges and VLANs: what changes in your homelab
article.description: Understand the difference between a Proxmox Linux bridge and VLAN segmentation before changing a homelab network.
article.dek: A Linux bridge connects virtual machines; a VLAN divides the network into segments. They solve different problems.

sections.heading: A Linux bridge connects guests
paragraphs: Proxmox VE uses Linux bridge interfaces to connect virtual machines to networks. The installer typically creates a bridge named vmbr0 and connects it to a physical network interface.
Think of the bridge as a software switch. Guests attached to the bridge can use the attached network, subject to the host and external network configuration.
bullets: Identify which physical interface your bridge uses.
Verify the host's management address and gateway before changes.
Do not assume that adding a second bridge automatically creates a separate physical network.

sections.heading: A VLAN separates network segments
paragraphs: VLANs distinguish separate Layer 2 broadcast domains using tags. Proxmox documents several ways to connect guests to VLANs, including VLAN-aware Linux bridges and per-VLAN bridge interfaces.
A VLAN-aware bridge can carry tagged guest traffic, but the connected switch and any upstream ports must also be configured to carry the intended VLANs.
bullets: List the VLAN IDs you actually need.
Check the switch port configuration and tagging requirements.
Plan management access before editing a remote host's networking.

sections.heading: Practical homelab decision
paragraphs: If all guests share one trusted LAN, a conventional Linux bridge may be sufficient. Use VLAN segmentation when you need distinct guest, management, or lab networks and can configure the full path consistently.
Proxmox supports web-interface changes and direct network configuration edits. Use a maintenance window and an out-of-band recovery plan for changes that could interrupt remote management.
bullets: Bridge: how guests attach to a network.
VLAN: which isolated Layer 2 segment their traffic belongs to.
Check the Proxmox version and current documentation before applying configuration.
